title: Mets designate reliever Luis García for assignment
content:
NEW YORK — In the first acknowledgement of an offseason move that hasn’t worked out as planned, the New York Mets have designated right-handed reliever Luis García for assignment. The veteran García, who had been signed over the winter to a major-league deal worth $1.75 million, posted a 7.11 ERA over six appearances.

New York recalled righty Joey Gerber from Triple-A Syracuse to take García’s spot on the roster.

“We needed an arm, especially the way we used the bullpen the last couple of nights,” manager Carlos Mendoza said Sunday morning.

Kodai Senga didn’t make it past the third inning Saturday. Clay Holmes departed Friday’s game in the sixth with an injury. New York had already used its two long men, Sean Manaea and Tobias Myers, on Wednesday and Friday, which stretched the pen more behind Senga on Saturday.

Signed as a middle reliever with the chance to pitch in some high-leverage spots, García had a couple of rough early outings. He allowed two runs on three hits on Opening Day and three runs on three hits in a third of an inning earlier this week against the Arizona Diamondbacks.

The Mets had struggled early this season with their bullpen’s inflexible configuration. The team has wanted to keep Manaea stretched out, to use Myers in longer stints, and to avoid back-to-back outings for Brooks Raley. The only two pitchers with options have been Myers and Huascar Brazobán, both of whom have pitched well. That prevented the Mets from using the revolving-door approach they employed last season to provide greater bullpen depth; the 2025 Mets and Atlanta Braves set a major-league record by using 46 pitchers.

It was thus likely, if not inevitable, that this move with García was going to happen at some point this season.

Gerber, acquired from the Tampa Bay Rays in November after they designated him for assignment, appeared in two big-league games for Tampa Bay last season — his first major-league action since 2020. He appeared in four games for Syracuse this season, allowing three earned runs and six hits in five innings.

The Mets’ offseason overhaul is off to a rocky start. They enter Sunday’s series finale with the Athletics on a four-game losing streak and in fourth place in the NL East at 7-8, before heading west on a difficult road trip to Dodger Stadium and Wrigley Field.
